Description

AMOS STEAM Clubs are afterschool programs offered at participating schools each school year. From tinkering to astronaut training, students participate in hands on exploration of science. AMOS educators are not teachers, we’re facilitators; our clubs are guided by the students and their natural scientific inquiry. We’re here to show students that science isn’t just for school, it’s everywhere and all around you–and it’s beyond fun!

AMOS has worked with many schools over the past decade. if AMOS STEAM Club is not currently offered at your child’s school, pease make a request with your school’s administration, your request is the best way to expand our reach to more students.

Description

Swift App School’s App Development Summer Camp empowers teens to learn coding and develop apps for the iPhone and other Apple platforms. We spend the week of App Camp building a traditional app, an Augmented Reality project for the VisionPro and a 2D mobile game. Students will also learn how to prompt AI to help them enhance their app’s features along the way. While learning important Computer Science concepts, students will build multiple apps using Apple’s Xcode development software. Join us for an exciting week of creative exploration and fun!

Our trained student teachers support student learning throughout the week. Snacks, drinks and lunches are provided each day for all students.

Description

DREAM (Dedicated, Responsible, Enthusiastic, After-School, Mentors) is a youth-centered leadership development program for 10th through 12th graders. DREAM members help support ACSF’s mission and facilitate programming for middle schoolers as near-peer mentors in the IRL after-school program at Asheville Middle School. This paid internship experience is complemented by professional development workshops that give DREAM members the skills they need to be excellent leaders and mentors. The DREAM team is a supportive space for students to learn, grow, and connect. Monthly “just for fun” outings provide opportunities for community building and social support. During the summer, the DREAM team supports middle schoolers attending the IRL/WORX Project summer camps.

Girls on the Run of WNC is a nonprofit program that inspires 3rd to 8th-grade girls to be joyful, healthy, and confident. Coaches lead each session focusing on skills, such as persistence, goal setting, managing emotions, resolving conflicts, and building friendships, with each practice integrating running and movement games designed to reinforce the lesson of the day.

Description

In Real Life (IRL) After-School provides high quality, hands-on, equitable, and accessible after school experiences for all Asheville City Schools middle school students. IRL is committed to ensuring that all students have access to opportunities which allow them to explore their interests and ignite their creativity. IRL operates on an affordable sliding scale of $0-$100/per club and partners with Asheville City Schools transportation to provide bussing around the city and in the evenings. By collaborating with 50+ community organizations and professionals, IRL has developed unique youth-informed programs to meet the demands of Asheville City Schools middle school students.

Description

Jones Afterschool provides interest-based clubs, in order to prioritize extra-curricular enrichment opportunities for students to explore new topics and skills with their friends peers. We offer scholarships for students with financial need, as well as the option for later pickup until 5:15. We partner with organizations like the Asheville Museum of Science and Sun Soo, as well as community members, and Jones staff to provide a variety of clubs that encourage students to share new experiences with students across grade levels, and often learn skills they usually wouldn’t be able to practice during the school day! Dungeons and Dragons sessions for 3rd-5th grade students have been our most popular groups this past year!

Description

Marvelous Math Club is an community after school club that uses a unique partnership model for math learning in community. A partnership of UNCA, ACS and HACA, requested by residents of PVA, MMC celebrates and centers the experiences of its elementary-age students (Math Leaders). Our Club creates a space at the PVA Community Center where Math Leaders feel safe, emotionally supported and excited to engage in Math. Math Champions support the Math Leaders with homework completion, math games and demonstrating math leadership.
